requirement: Let an order own its lines so that replacing the lines deletes the old rows and deleting the order deletes its lines, validating every quantity before any change and committing each operation.
skeleton: Order and Line declarative models joined by a one-to-many relationship with cascade all, delete-orphan and a non-nullable foreign key, a _load helper raising LookupError, replace_lines validating then clearing and extending the collection, and delete_order deleting through the session.
caption: Parent-owned children with SQLAlchemy 2.0 typed declarative mapping. Order has an id, a customer name and a lines relationship declared with back_populates, cascade="all, delete-orphan" and order_by Line.id; Line has an id, a non-nullable order_id ForeignKey to orders.id, a sku, a qty and the back-reference. Because of delete-orphan, a line removed from order.lines is deleted from the table instead of having its foreign key set to NULL, and because of the all cascade, deleting the order deletes its lines. A private _load helper uses session.get and raises LookupError saying order N not found. replace_lines(session, order_id, items) takes a sequence of sku and quantity pairs, first raises ValueError saying the quantity for that sku must be at least 1 when any quantity is below 1, and only then clears the collection, extends it with new Line objects, commits and returns the order. delete_order(session, order_id) deletes the order and commits. The fixture asserts that replacing lines leaves only the new lines in order and four rows in the table, that deleting an order survives a rollback and leaves only the other order's line, that a zero quantity raises ValueError with the original lines untouched, and that unknown ids raise LookupError.

plan.intent: Keep order lines consistent with their order
constraints: Replacing an order's lines deletes the old line rows
Deleting an order deletes its lines
Lines are listed in insertion order
A quantity below 1 raises ValueError before any line changes

rationale.teaches: cascade="all, delete-orphan" on a one-to-many relationship so collection removal and parent deletion delete child rows, with validation done before mutating the collection.
rationale.why: The default cascade nulls the foreign key of removed children, which either leaves orphan rows or fails on a non-null column, and validating mid-mutation leaves a half-cleared collection behind.

ops.docstring: Orders whose lines live and die with them through cascade rules.

ops.stmt:
from sqlalchemy.orm import (
    DeclarativeBase,
    Mapped,
    Session,
    mapped_column,
    relationship,
)

ops.source:
class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    """Declarative base for this module's tables."""

class Order(Base):
    """An order owning its lines."""

    __tablename__ = "orders"

    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    customer: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(50))
    lines: Mapped[list["Line"]] = relationship(
        back_populates="order", cascade="all, delete-orphan", order_by="Line.id"
    )

class Line(Base):
    """One product line; it cannot exist without its order."""

    __tablename__ = "lines"

    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    order_id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(ForeignKey("orders.id"), nullable=False)
    sku: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(20))
    qty: Mapped[int]
    order: Mapped[Order] = relationship(back_populates="lines")

def delete_order(session: Session, order_id: int) -> None:
    """Delete an order together with its lines and commit."""
    session.delete(_load(session, order_id))
    session.commit()

candidates.why_wrong: Without delete-orphan the cleared lines get a NULL order_id, which the non-null column rejects.
The default save-update, merge cascade neither deletes removed lines nor the lines of a deleted order.
A quantity of zero passes the check because only negative quantities are rejected.
The collection is cleared before validation, so a rejected quantity leaves the order with no lines.
delete_order only flushes, so a rollback brings the order and its lines back.
